# Answer to HAWK's ask: the Gulf of Finland ship (cards 20261121-003 item 8, 20261123-006 item 3)

| Question | Answer | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Vessel | **Sparta II, IMO 9160994, Russian-flagged roll-on/roll-off cargo ship**, associated with Oboronlogistika (Russian state-linked military logistics); US-sanctioned 2022, on Ukraine's list this year | gCaptain article (page read); Marine Insight 11/23 (page read); sanctions dates from a search summary |
| Type | **Cargo (ro-ro), NOT a tanker.** 'History of transporting military equipment' | gCaptain |
| When, where | Sat 11/21, detected about 08:40 to 08:50 local, about 50 km west of Gogland (Suursaari), **international waters**; lost steering and drifted into Finnish territorial waters south of Loviisa | gCaptain citing Finland's Ministry of Defence |
| Route | Sailing to Kaliningrad | Marine Insight; the Leningrad governor said two drones (search summary) |
| Attacker | **Finnish armed forces spokesperson Aki-Mauri Huhtinen: Ukraine 'likely' responsible**, reason for targeting unclear (Kyiv Independent citing Reuters, published 11/21, updated 11/22). A 'Zelensky confirms' headline appeared in search results: reported, page not read | Kyiv Independent page read |
| Outcome | 16 crew evacuated, no injuries reported, no environmental damage detected at 14:58 local 11/21; Russian rescue vessel Murman began the tow on the afternoon of 11/22 after two days of firefighting, toward St. Petersburg; Finnish Border Guard ended its mission when the ship left Finland's economic zone | gCaptain; Marine Insight |
| Side events | a Russian helicopter suspected of entering Finnish airspace near Loviisa, up to 4.1 km (Finnish defence minister Häkkänen); temporary Finnish sea and air restrictions in the eastern Gulf | gCaptain |

- **Limits:** the FT and BBC pages HAWK named were not read; the identification rests on three outlets that name one ship with the same date, place and route. Attribution is Finland's 'likely', not an established fact.
- **So what:** HAWK said a merchant TANKER struck in the Ukraine-side Baltic campaign would block OSPREY's 11/27 kill of C3 limb 1. This ship is a military-linked cargo ship, not a tanker. Whether it counts under the limb's letter is OSPREY's grade, not WALTER's.
